players.product: memory (DRAM / NAND) and display-driver assembly & test

quarterly_data.signal: ChipMOS 20-F customer concentration: its top five customers collectively accounted for 61% of 2025 revenue, and its top three accounted for approximately 23%, 15% and 9% (24%, 11% and 11% in 2024; 25%, 13% and 9% in 2023). The filing names them only as Customer A (NT$5,393,013 thousand, 23% of 2025 revenue), Customer K (NT$3,673,340 thousand, 15%) and Customer B (NT$2,209,678 thousand, 9%). ChipMOS says it focuses on sales to key customers through long-term service agreements and expects to keep relying on a relatively limited number of customers.
quarterly_data.figure: top five customers 61%; Customer A 23%, Customer K 15%, Customer B 9% (2025)

quarterly_data.signal: ChipMOS 20-F: driven by the strong rebound in the memory market since the second half of 2025, ChipMOS finalized a long-term 3-year memory wafer test capacity take-or-pay contract in the beginning of 2026 (the customer is not named). In the fourth quarter of 2021 it had settled a long-term 3-year capacity secure agreement with a customer for high-end wafer test for OLED and other display panel driver demand.
quarterly_data.figure: 3-year memory wafer test capacity take-or-pay contract (beginning of 2026)

quarterly_data.signal: ChipMOS 20-F full-year 2025 results: revenue NT$23,932.9 million (US$762.9 million) versus NT$22,695.9 million in 2024; gross profit NT$2,592.4 million, an overall gross margin of 10.8% (13.0% in 2024); operating profit NT$1,142.7 million and profit for the year NT$550.6 million.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 revenue NT$23,932.9 million; gross margin 10.8%

quarterly_data.signal: ChipMOS 20-F segment revenue, testing services for memory and logic/mixed-signal semiconductors: NT$5,677.9 million in 2025 (US$181.0 million), 23.7% of revenue, versus NT$4,967.9 million in 2024 (XBRL: +14.3% YoY); segment gross margin 22.1% (19.2% in 2024).
quarterly_data.figure: testing NT$5,677.9 million (+14.3% YoY); gross margin 22.1%

quarterly_data.signal: ChipMOS 20-F segment revenue, assembly services for memory and logic/mixed-signal semiconductors: NT$6,827.4 million in 2025 (US$217.6 million), 28.6% of revenue, versus NT$5,390.4 million in 2024 (XBRL: +26.7% YoY); the segment's gross margin was -1.6% (-11.2% in 2024).
quarterly_data.figure: assembly NT$6,827.4 million (+26.7% YoY); gross margin -1.6%

quarterly_data.signal: ChipMOS 20-F segment revenue, bumping services: NT$5,557.7 million in 2025 (US$177.2 million), 23.2% of revenue, versus NT$5,018.6 million in 2024 (XBRL: +10.7% YoY); segment gross margin 18.0% (19.0% in 2024).
quarterly_data.figure: bumping NT$5,557.7 million (+10.7% YoY); gross margin 18.0%

quarterly_data.signal: ChipMOS 20-F capex: capital expenditures were NT$3,666.1 million (US$116.9 million) in 2025 versus NT$5,451.4 million in 2024; by segment, 2025 purchases of property, plant and equipment were testing NT$1,819,916 thousand, assembly NT$690,525 thousand, display panel driver (LCDD) NT$814,160 thousand and bumping NT$341,461 thousand. Capital expenditures contracted for but not provided for were NT$1,321,008 thousand at December 31, 2025. A substantial portion of capex, primarily for assembly and testing equipment, is denominated in US dollars with much of the remainder in Japanese yen.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 capex NT$3,666.1 million; contracted, not provided NT$1,321,008 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: ChipMOS 20-F equipment base and suppliers: as of February 28, 2026 ChipMOS operated 702 testers for memory and logic/mixed-signal semiconductors and 955 wire bonders, and for display panel driver semiconductors 10 steppers and 17 sputters for gold bumping, 105 inner-lead bonders and 731 testers. It purchases wire bonders principally from Shinkawa Co., Ltd. and Kulicke & Soffa Industries Inc., and bought TCP-related assembly equipment from Shibaura Mechatronics Corp. It has no binding supply agreements with its equipment suppliers and buys on a purchase order basis; some equipment has been in short supply, with order-to-delivery lead times in excess of six months.
quarterly_data.figure: 702 memory/logic testers; 955 wire bonders; 731 display-driver testers (Feb 28, 2026)

contracts.signal: ChipMOS 20-F: ChipMOS purchases its testers for memory and logic/mixed-signal semiconductors from Advantest Corporation (it operated 702 such testers as of February 28, 2026), and it also purchased additional TCP-related testers for display panel driver semiconductors from Advantest.
